messages.author: de3190e0e6f4a690
messages.subject: Interaction between fixed effects (Inlabru/INLA)
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to include an interaction term, between land-use (fixed effect using a continuous scale) and forest quality. 
Both are modelled linearly, though land-use is more of an indicator variable.

I've done some searching but haven't been able to find any information on how to actually write the code. Does anyone have any advice on how to do this?

Thanks for your help,
Sol

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Interaction between fixed effects (Inlabru/INLA)
parts:
the formula supports the format like

u*v

for variables u v, which will expand to

u + v + I(u*v)

for continuous reponse or by factors, if one is a factor.

you can mix this with a f(), like

f(idx, u, model="...)

which will multiply the contribution from f[idx] with u[idx], so you get

u[idx] * f[idx]

as a contribution, but this is only for continous u. if that is a
factor, you have to do that manually.

H

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Interaction between fixed effects (Inlabru/INLA)
parts:
Hi,

as you clarified elsewhere this is for inlabru, and that the covariate
information is stored as two rasters, with one continuous and the
other (functionally) an 0/1 indicator.

First, convert the functionally 0/1 variable to actual 0/1 values, so
they can be used in calculations.
If these had been ordinary covariates, A and B, stored in the data
object, you could have used
A + B + AB(map = A*B, model="linear")
but as these are stored as rasters, that, as well as the following,
would _not_ work,
A(map=A, model="linear") + B(map=B, model="linear") + AB(map=A*B,
model="linear")
since A*B as far as I know isn't defined for rasters in the way needed for this.

Instead, you can create a new raster, AB, that contains the pointwise
products of A and B, as a raster.
The last component is then + AB(map = AB, model="linear")

Alternatively, you could define a function fun(x, y) that evaluated
and returned the product of A and B at locations (x,y),
but the new raster approaches seems easier.

Finn
